strategy.summary: Reproduce the native-complex NaN-component bug in pandas array_equivalent by building pandas from source at the buggy commit 61cbe5f9c92c and running the developer's new parametrized test test_array_equivalent_complex_nan_component in pandas/tests/dtypes/test_missing.py. The test should fail on the buggy revision for native complex with dtype_equal=True, where the float-pair fastpath returns False for 1+nanj vs 2+nanj, and pass on the fixed revision, where the numpy comparison with isnan handles whole-element NA. The transition is the whole success criterion.

system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang) capable of building pandas Cython extensions
build_commands: pip install cython numpy python-dateutil meson-python meson versioneer pytest hypothesis
pinned_because: NumPy, python-dateutil, tzdata and Cython have no documented constraint and no era table entry, so no version is pinned; pip resolves current releases and the strategy relies on the repo's pyproject build-system requirements for the build toolchain.
Python version is null in the evidence, so no interpreter version is pinned; use one supported by the buggy commit's pyproject.toml.
tzdata is only required on Windows/Emscripten and is not needed on Linux for this test.

strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/dtypes/test_missing.py::test_array_equivalent_complex_nan_component (parametrized over dtype in [c16, c8, >c16, >c8] and dtype_equal in [True, False])
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 61cbe5f9c92c the test fails: for native dtypes c16 and c8 with dtype_equal=True, the first assertion array_equivalent(np.array([1+nanj]), np.array([2+nanj]), dtype_equal=True) returns False and raises AssertionError, while dtype_equal=False passes. On the fixed revision (the PR #66323 change routing complex through (left == right) | (np.isnan(left) & np.isnan(right))).all()) every parametrized case passes, including all byte-swapped >c16 and >c8 cases.
risks: The bug requires a native complex dtype (c16/c8) with dtype_equal=True to reach the float-pair fastpath; the byte-swapped >c16/>c8 cases may already pass on the buggy revision, so the test is expected to fail only on the native parametrizations. Do not treat a partially failing parametrization as a setup error.

Build is required: the Cython extensions must be compiled at each checkout. Switching between buggy and fixed commits needs a rebuild, or an editable meson-python install will rebuild on import; a stale build can make both revisions appear to behave the same.

The bug is IEEE-754 NaN handling and is not architecture-specific in the evidence, so no special platform or sanitizer is assumed. If the buggy behaviour is not reproduced on the local platform, check the NumPy version and compiler rather than the architecture.
The PR body references GH#66160 in the test comment while the PR is #66323; the issue number is not a reproduction input and does not affect the test selection.

NumPy version is unbounded in the evidence, so a much newer or older NumPy may change complex comparison or isnan behaviour in unrelated tests; the selected test is narrow but the build may fail if the NumPy ABI does not match the buggy commit's build requirements.

oracle.reference_source: test assertions in the developer test diff and the PR body expected behaviour
oracle.why: The checks are exact boolean equivalence results (True or False) from array_equivalent, not approximate numerical comparisons.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On 61cbe5f9c92c, the first assert array_equivalent(left, right, dtype_equal=True) for native complex128/complex64 gets False from the float-pair fastpath, which compares real and imaginary parts independently and so sees 1 != 2 despite the NaN imaginary parts, so the test raises AssertionError.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision, the numpy comparison with whole-element NA treats each pair with a NaN component as NA, so all four assertion groups return True or False as expected for both dtype_equal values and all four dtypes.
